buildlog.body:
I put the site through Dev0 today. Claude audited every file against the six tests.

| Test | Result |
| -------- | -------- |
| Less | Pass |
| Separate | Partial |
| Legibility | Pass |
| Native | Partial |
| Beneficiary | Fail |
| Control | Fail |

The code was lean: no dependencies and no build step. The problem was where it ran. Every page was assembled in the visitor's browser, the one runtime I don't control. Without JavaScript, a page was blank, and a shared Work link previewed with a generic title.

What changed:

- The local CMS now writes finished HTML for every Work, Case Study and Letter page. That breaks Dev0's no-compile-step rule, so the exception is written into CLAUDE.md, along with the alternatives we rejected.
- Drafts stay with the CMS and never deploy. Before, they were hidden on the page but readable in the source.
- Fonts are self-hosted instead of loaded from Google.

>A strong pass in one never excuses a failure in another.

casestudies.title: Does My Local CMS Work?
casestudies.description: Short description of the case study.

sections.label: Opportunity
sections.body:
Adding content to my personal website via html and js files is arduous!

User friendly content management will make the site easier, and more fun to run.

sections.label: Solution
sections.body:
Create a local CMS. 
Preview the content changes locally then merge via GitHub to the production site.

sections.label: Wins
sections.body:
Claude Code built it in 10 minutes.

I have autonomy and no third party dependancies.

sections.label: Learning
sections.body: It seems almost to easy. It's too early to determine if it was a success. This is a test post.
